advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a bound-but-principal-less signer should fail closed (or explicitly document the env fallback) rather than silently reading REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID.
evidence: _opcert_signing.py:219-224: `effective = binding if binding is not None else _current_binding()` then `if effective is not None and effective.principal and effective.principal.strip(): return ...` else falls to `os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID")`
keyprov.py:76 `return OpcertSigner(key_path=copy_path, principal=cfg.env_id, runtime_dir=runtime_dir)` — no validation that cfg.env_id is set
jobs.py docstring claims signing binds "WITHOUT setting REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH / REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID in the process env" (jobs.py:82)
advisory.finding: When a signer is bound but its `principal` is empty/None (e.g. `cfg.env_id` unset), `opcert_principal` falls through to reading `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` (and then `.env-id`) from the process environment, despite the module's stated invariant that a bound gate never re-reads env; `compose_signer` sets `principal=cfg.env_id` without requiring it to be non-empty.
scenarios: A deployment that mounts a key file but omits REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID: the composed signer's principal is None, so the DSSE principal silently resolves from process env / store .env-id rather than the composed binding.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a non-root USER to Dockerfile.opcert so the op-cert signing service does not run as root.
evidence: infra/compose/Dockerfile.opcert has no `USER` directive; CMD is `["uvicorn", "rebar.opcert_service.app:app", ...]` running as the default root user
The service handles the passphrase-free Ed25519 private key: `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH: "/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key"` (docker-compose.yml:271) mounted `:ro`
keyprov.py copies the key into `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rebar-opcert-")` at 0700 (keyprov.py:67-68) — least-privilege would run this as a dedicated non-root uid
advisory.finding: Dockerfile.opcert defines no non-root USER, so the op-cert service (which now reads a mounted private key and copies it into a 0700 runtime dir) runs as root; a compromised process runs with full container-root privileges and can read the bind-mounted key regardless of its 0600 mode.
advisory.suggested_fix: Create a dedicated unprivileged user in Dockerfile.opcert (e.g. `RUN useradd -r -u 10001 opcert` then `USER opcert`), ensuring the mounted key is readable by that uid.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/verify the intended blast-radius when opcert-ed25519-key is blank (crash-loop vs. disabled) and document/guard it (e.g. don't start opcert, or a longer restart backoff).
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh:136-137 `opcert-ed25519-key is blank — wrote an EMPTY ${opcert_key_path}; the op-cert gate service will fail startup key composition`
docker-compose.yml:257 `restart: unless-stopped`

keyprov.py `_validate_key_file` raises `OpcertKeyError` for an empty/malformed key (keyprov.py:72, compose_signer), and app.py lifespan calls `compose_signer(app.state.config)` BEFORE serving, so an invalid key aborts every startup
advisory.finding: When the SSM slot `opcert-ed25519-key` is blank, fetch-secrets.sh writes an EMPTY key file that fails compose_signer validation, and the compose service is `restart: unless-stopped`, so the opcert service enters a crash-loop instead of a clean disabled/degraded state.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY inline-env source is intended and, if kept, document that it must not be used in the deployed compose environment (file path only).
evidence: config.py `_private_key_env()` reads `os.environ.get("REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY")` and returns it VERBATIM
keyprov.py `_read_source_key` returns `private_key.encode("utf-8")` as a valid key source (keyprov.py:95)
module docstring frames it as `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY, compat` fallback — a private key in an env var is visible via /proc/<pid>/environ, `docker inspect`, and process listings
advisory.finding: The `REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` inline-PEM source path lets the raw Ed25519 private key be supplied through a process environment variable, a secrets-in-env anti-pattern that the file-based path was introduced to avoid.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the deployed bind-mount source is guaranteed 0600 (and consider whether the read-only ro mount + container-root read makes the 0o077 check reject legitimate deploys).
evidence: keyprov.py:108-112 rejects the key when `st.st_mode & 0o077` (any group/other bit set)
fetch-secrets.sh:132 `chmod 600 "${opcert_key_path}"` sets the mode at materialization time only

docker-compose.yml:290 `- ./opcert-ed25519-key:/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key:ro` — the container sees whatever mode/ownership the host file carries at start; no test asserts the mount is 0600 (test_opcert_deploy_infra only checks env keys)
advisory.finding: compose_signer validates the MOUNTED source file is 0600-or-stricter, but nothing in the IaC asserts the host file ./opcert-ed25519-key ownership/mode as seen inside the container; a host umask/ownership drift makes the group/other bits fail the `st.st_mode & 0o077` check and blocks startup.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that compose_signer rejects a key_path with mode 0o644 (or any group/other bits set) with OpcertKeyError.
evidence: keyprov.py:108-112 `if st.st_mode & 0o077: raise OpcertKeyError(... must be 0600 or stricter ...)`
module docstring lists `too-permissive` as an AC1 rejection case (keyprov.py:40)

search_files for `0o644` in tests/unit returned `(no matches)`; heldout AC1 tests (test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:119-161) cover no-source/both-set/unreadable/non-Ed25519/garbage but never a mode-too-permissive source
advisory.finding: The too-permissive-mode rejection branch is untested: no test composes a signer from a key file with group/other permission bits set (mode & 0o077), so the security contract that a 0644/group-readable key source is rejected has no regression guard.
scenarios: A refactor drops or inverts the mode check and a world/group-readable deployment key is silently accepted — no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py, write an Ed25519 key, chmod it 0o644, and assert compose_signer(cfg) raises OpcertKeyError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that compose_signer rejects a passphrase-protected Ed25519 key (ssh-keygen -N 'pass') with OpcertKeyError.
evidence: keyprov.py:145-149 `if proc.returncode != 0: raise OpcertKeyError('... malformed, encrypted (passphrase-protected) ...')`
module docstring lists `encrypted` as a distinct AC1 rejection case (keyprov.py:40)
heldout `test_invalid_source_rejected_before_any_job` (test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:154-161) uses `bad.write_text('not a private key')` — a malformed file, not an encrypted valid key
advisory.finding: The encrypted/passphrase-protected key rejection branch is not distinctly tested: the only malformed-key test uses a garbage text file, but no test feeds a well-formed but passphrase-protected Ed25519 key to exercise the ssh-keygen returncode!=0 path.
scenarios: A change to the ssh-keygen invocation (e.g. dropping `-P ""`) that lets a passphrase-protected key through would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that compose_signer composes a working signer from cfg.private_key (inline PEM) alone and signs successfully.
evidence: keyprov.py:88-95 `_read_source_key`: `if key_path: return _read_path_source(key_path)` else `return private_key.encode('utf-8')`
search_files `private_key` in tests/unit shows keyprov's inline source only at test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:129 (the both-set rejection); no test passes private_key alone to compose_signer
config.py:_private_key_env returns the value VERBATIM (not stripped) — an untested newline-significance contract

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives opcert_service.app.lifespan: an invalid key raises before queue/worker creation, and a valid one calls signer.cleanup() on shutdown.
evidence: app.py:56 `app.state.signer = compose_signer(app.state.config)` with comment 'the app never begins serving' on an invalid source
app.py:90-94 shutdown calls `signer.cleanup()`
search_files `opcert_service.app` and `app.state.signer` in tests found no lifespan test (only Dockerfile CMD grep at test_opcert_service.py:361); review_bot lifespan is tested but opcert's is not
advisory.finding: The opcert service `lifespan` is entirely untested: neither the fail-closed AC1 ordering (compose the signer BEFORE any queue/worker creation, so an invalid key aborts startup before serving) nor the shutdown `signer.cleanup()` has any test.
scenarios: A refactor that moves signer composition after queue/worker startup (breaking fail-closed) or drops signer.cleanup() on shutdown (leaking the process-owned key copy) would pass all tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `async with lifespan(fake_app)` with a stub config: assert OpcertKeyError propagates for an invalid source and that app.state.signer.runtime_dir is removed after exit.
